title: Application of AI and Deep Learning to Genomic and Transcriptomic Data Analysis in Cancer
summary: Application of AI and deep learning methods to genomic and transcriptomic data analysis in cancer.

context.degree: B.S. Business Administration for Tech Companies

researchQuestion: When we try to predict how long a breast-cancer patient will survive from their tumour's gene expression, do modern deep survival networks actually beat a well-regularised classical Cox model — or do they just look more impressive?

data.dataset: TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq (RSEM) expression and clinical data from cBioPortal, study brca_tcga_pub2015 (Breast Invasive Carcinoma, TCGA, Cell 2015)
data.genes: 20,440 raw; 18,492 after the low-expression filter; 1,000 selected
data.endpoint: Overall survival, administratively censored at 60 months

method.featureSelection: Low-expression filter (genes with more than 80% zero values removed), then limma differential expression and univariate Cox screening, fitted on the training split only
method.validation: Fixed patient split shared by all models (splits.json); hyperparameters chosen without the test set (k-fold cross-validation for Cox and Random Survival Forest models, validation set and grid search for DeepSurv and Cox-nnet); fixed random seed 42
method.evaluation: Harrell's concordance index (C-index) on held-out test patients; Kaplan–Meier curves and log-rank test on median-split high- and low-risk groups
method.interpretability: SHAP attributions with 50 bootstrap resamples for DeepSurv and Cox-nnet; gene-set enrichment against GO, KEGG and Reactome with GSEApy; STRING protein-protein interaction cross-check; Random Survival Forest minimal-depth interaction analysis

findings: DeepSurv achieved the best discriminative performance (C-index of approximately 0.82).
DeepSurv was the only model to produce a statistically significant risk stratification, outperforming both the linear Cox models and the Random Survival Forest.
DeepSurv and Cox-nnet shared 257 prognostic genes in the bootstrap SHAP consensus.
limitations: The test set has about one hundred patients and no confidence interval is reported.
The neural networks' loss curves show overfitting.
There is no external validation cohort.
